listings.name: 10 Copy-Paste AI Prompts for Teachers
listings.title: 10 Copy-Paste AI Prompts for Teachers | ChatGPT Time Savers | Free
listings.description:
Ten AI prompts that work on the first try, for the tasks that actually eat your evenings: parent emails, leveled passages, rubrics, quiz questions, and newsletter blurbs.

Copy, paste, change the bracket, done. No account, no signup, no tool required beyond whatever chatbot you already have.

Built and audited by two certified teachers with 20+ combined years in classrooms. If these save you an evening, our full PD sessions are in the store.

listings.name: The One Hard Rule Poster
listings.title: AI Student Privacy Poster | The One Hard Rule | Staff Room Printable | Free
listings.description:
One rule, printed big enough to end the argument: never put student personally identifiable information into a public AI tool. Not a name. Not a detail. Ever.

Print it for the staff room, the copier, or the back of your own door. It covers every tool your staff will ever use, including the ones that do not exist yet.

Built and audited by two certified teachers.

listings.name: AI Tool Safety Checklist
listings.title: AI Tool Safety Checklist for Teachers | Vet Any AI Tool in 5 Minutes | Free
listings.description:
A new AI tool lands in your inbox every week. This is what to check before you or your students touch it: what it does with data, who owns what you type, what it asks for, and the questions worth taking to your district.

One page, five minutes, works on any tool.

Built and audited by two certified teachers.

listings.name: Talking to Parents About AI
listings.title: Talking to Parents About AI | Family Communication Guide for Teachers | Free
listings.description:
Plain answers to the questions families actually ask: is my child using AI, is that cheating, is their data safe, and what is the school doing about it.

Ready to send, ready to say out loud at conferences, written so nobody needs a technology background to follow it.

Built and audited by two certified teachers.

listings.name: AI Readiness Checklist for School Leaders
listings.title: AI Readiness Checklist for School Leaders | Principal Planning Tool | Free
listings.description:
Where your building actually stands on AI, in one honest page: what your staff is already doing, what is written down, what is not, and what to do first.

Built for principals and instructional coaches who need a starting point rather than a strategy deck.

Built and audited by two certified teachers.

listings.name: 20 De-Identification Drills
listings.title: AI Student Privacy Practice | 20 De-Identification Drills | FERPA | Free
listings.description:
The one AI skill every teacher needs and nobody practices: getting real help from AI without ever putting a student's identity into it.

Twenty before-and-after prompt makeovers, from parent emails to IEP-adjacent requests to the sneaky no-name prompts that still identify a child. Cover the answer, rewrite it in your head, compare. Ten seconds per prompt by the last page.

Includes the three de-identification moves, the ten-second test, and a printable pocket checklist. Every name is fictional; the unsafe examples exist for practice.

Built and audited by two certified teachers.

listings.name: AI Vocabulary for Teachers
listings.title: AI Vocabulary for Teachers | 30 AI Terms in Plain English | Free Cheat Sheet
listings.description:
Thirty AI terms explained the way you'd explain them to a colleague in the hallway — no computer science degree, no marketing spin.

INSIDE (2 pages): the basics (prompt, chatbot, LLM, iterating) · how it actually works, honestly (hallucination, bias, training data, context window) · the school-safety words every educator needs (PII, FERPA, COPPA, de-identification, district-approved vs. public tools, why AI detectors are unreliable) · and the buzzwords decoded (prompt engineering, AI literacy, agents, wrappers).

listings.name: The 10-Minute AI Habit
listings.title: 10 Minute AI Habit for Teachers | Weekly Planner & Prompt Tracker | Free
listings.description:
You don't learn AI in a summer workshop — you learn it ten minutes at a time, on real tasks, until it's just how you work.

INSIDE (2 pages): the habit in three moves (same slot every week, one task, save what worked) · an eight-week starter ladder with a ready prompt for each week — parent messages, leveling texts, exit tickets, rubrics, sub plans, and your first reusable template · a printable tracker that lives in your planner.

Every prompt is safe as written: no student information ever goes into an AI tool.

Built and audited by two certified teachers.

listings.name: Don't Type That: Student PII Poster
listings.title: Student Data Privacy Poster | 10 Things Never to Type Into AI | FERPA Friendly
listings.description:
The poster for every wall near a device: ten things that count as student PII — names, IDs, IEP status, medical details, behavior stories, one-of-a-kind combinations — and the habit that replaces them: describe the need, not the child.

INSIDE (2 pages): the printable poster (schoolhouse navy, reads from across the room) · a one-page guide with the three de-identification moves, a risky-vs-safe prompt table, and the ten-second test before you press enter.

Hang it by the copier, drop it in the PD folder, send it to the colleague who types first and thinks later.

Built and audited by two certified teachers.

listings.name: Emergency Sub Plans with AI
listings.title: Emergency Sub Plans with AI | 15 Minute System & Prompts | Free for Teachers
listings.description:
For the 5:30 a.m. you hoped wouldn't come: you're sick, and the sub folder is three units out of date.

INSIDE (2 pages): the 15-minute system (run the master prompt, fix only what's wrong, send and go back to bed) · one master prompt that drafts a complete sub day for a stranger — bell-ringers, numbered directions, early-finisher tasks · four gap-fillers (no-tech backup, review day, day two, management notes) · and the once-a-semester list of what to keep printed, because seating charts and health notes belong in the folder, never in a chatbot.

Built and audited by two certified teachers.

listings.name: AI or Teacher? Delegation Poster
listings.title: AI or Teacher Poster | What to Delegate to ChatGPT | Free Decision Guide
listings.description:
The fastest teachers with AI decided once what it's for. This poster is that decision, on the wall: three questions that sort any task in seconds.

Does it touch a student's identity? Stays out. Is it a judgment about a child? Stays yours. Is it a drafting or formatting task? Delegate the draft — then edit like the professional you are.

INSIDE (2 pages): the printable decision poster · a one-page guide with the delegate list (letters home, leveled texts, rubrics, sub plans) and the never-delegate list (grades, IEP decisions, seating charts, what's worth teaching).

Built and audited by two certified teachers.

listings.name: Parent Message Makeovers

listings.description:
The hardest emails of the school year are the ones you rewrite four times at 9 p.m. This pack drafts every one of them in minutes — warm, factual, professional, and sounding like you.

INSIDE (7 pages, 12 makeovers): the everyday five (missing work, grade drops, positive news home, attendance patterns, homework help) · the hard four (behavior incidents, angry-email replies, tough conference requests, the AI/academic-honesty conversation) · the whole-class three (logistics chasers, welcoming a student back, end-of-term updates) · plus the four-part tone formula behind them all, a build-your-own template for scenario thirteen, and the read-aloud test before every send.

Every prompt is safe by design: no student names or personal details ever go into the AI — you describe the situation, the AI drafts to "a family," and personalization happens in your own email afterward.
